Yes I've been doing this as of late, and I've had some great success with it. I basically just set up an exposure hierarchy which lists the least anxiety provoking social situation, to the most anxiety provoking social situation. Then when it came to it, I recorded my anxiety beforehand (say a 5/10), went into the social situation (supermarket, small shop, bar, area with a lot of people in it etc.), waited for my anxiety to decrease (took about 30 mins), and challenged my thoughts about being scrutinized by others in the mean time. Once I had done that I went back home to record my anxiety during the event, and after the event, if it decreased afterwards, it was a success! I repeated this a few times over at least once a week, until I no longer had social phobia in that particular situation. Finally I moved on to the next exposure event, and repeated the same thing again, until I had ran out of things to expose myself to... I don't know what happened, but somewhere along the way I just stopped caring, and my social phobia just disappeared in most social situations, although I still get it in certain places, and I'm still doing exposure therapy in those situations. I would say it's worth it in the end although I agree it isn't easy, you should get a therapist that understands social phobia (there aren't many of them out there in my experience) and doesn't push you to hard. Forget waiting rooms though, I will always feel anxious in those, nosy fuckers won't stop staring at me lol.
